title: If Dogs Eat Turkey: Boneless and Fully Cooked, Says the ASPCA 🦃 (Things Living In Your House #70)
description:
Can dogs eat turkey? The ASPCA recommends sticking to your pet's normal diet on Thanksgiving. If you do decide to share a small bite of turkey, it says to make sure it's boneless and fully cooked: raw or undercooked turkey may contain salmonella, and poultry bones can be a major choking hazard. The FDA says dogs are notorious for helping themselves to the turkey carcass in the trash, and the bones can get stuck. Its advice: securely wrap up the table scraps and bones and put them in a trash bin your pets can't get into. The FDA adds that sharp pieces of bones can injure a dog's mouth, esophagus and stomach. General information, not advice for your dog: ask your vet.

#dogs #thanksgiving #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: ASPCA, Thanksgiving Safety Tips; FDA, Keep Your Dogs and Cats Safe From Holiday Hazards.
